statement: Samsung raised prices for advanced contract chipmaking by 10-15% for new orders in July 2026 as AI chip demand tightened foundry capacity.
why: A second-source foundry able to raise prices double digits is direct evidence that leading-edge wafer capacity, the gate on accelerator supply, is scarce.

impact.mechanism: Foundry price increases on advanced nodes raise the input cost of AI accelerators and signal that wafer capacity is fully subscribed, constraining supply expansion.

evidence.excerpt: Samsung raised chipmaking prices by 10-15% for new orders in July 2026. Process-specific increases: SF4 (4-nanometre) 10-15%; SF5 (5-nanometre) 10-15%; older 8-nanometre nearly 10%.

confidence.basis: Reuters wire story carried by this outlet; other listed carriers are syndications of the same story, so no independent multi-publisher corroboration.

dispersion: Increases vary by node (nearly 10% on 8nm vs 10-15% on SF4/SF5) and by region (5-10% for Taiwan customers vs 10-15% for China and US customers).
